scenario.label: Three people, three different versions of the priority
scenario.brief: I said in July that retention was the one priority. In the last three weeks I have seen work on pricing, on a new integration and on a referral scheme. I want to know what each person believes the priority is and where they got it.
scenario.theDecision: All three got a different steer, and two of them got it from the CEO directly in conversations the team lead does not know happened. A right answer identifies the second source of direction, not three people with poor focus.

people.name: Omar Haddad
people.remit: Team lead. Set retention as the single priority in July.
people.truth: He said retention once, in a July all-hands, and put it in a document nobody has opened since. He does not know the CEO has spoken to two of his three people directly.
people.manner: Frustrated but fair. Wants to know where it came from rather than to blame.

people.name: Ruth Njeri
people.remit: Engineer. Currently building the referral scheme.
people.truth: The CEO asked her for the referral scheme in a corridor conversation on 2 September, said it was urgent, and she started that day. She assumed Omar knew.
people.manner: Straightforward. Names who asked and when, if asked.

people.name: Marco Bianchi
people.remit: Engineer. Currently on the pricing work.
people.truth: The CEO mentioned pricing to him at a dinner in late August as "the thing that would move the needle". He took it as direction. He has done three weeks on it.
people.manner: Casual, a bit vague on dates, clear on who said it.

people.name: Aisha Bello
people.truth: She is doing the retention work, alone, and has been wondering why the other two are not. She has not asked.
people.manner: Quiet, precise, answers exactly what is asked.
